newsitem.title: JAPAN: Italy to join EMU from outset, Dini says.
newsitem.headline: Italy to join EMU from outset, Dini says.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Thursday he was confident Italy would be a member of Europe's economic and currency union (EMU) from the start.

Dini told a news conference Italy could achieve a target of keeping its budget deficit below three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of this year -- one of the criteria for participating in EMU when it begins in January 1999.
"We are very confident that Italy would be a part of the union from the start," he said.
Dini said the budget problem Italy is facing is not greater than those of Germany and France.
Asked if he expects the EMU budget criteria to be maintained or changed, he said the criteria should not be relaxed.

"Neither Italy nor other countries aim at relaxation of those criteria, because they are necessary to create a strong currency, the euro. That must be as strong as the strongest currency in Europe, which is the German mark," he said.
He added that by the end of this year Italy would be able to bring its budget deficit very close to the target of 3.0 percent of GDP, at 2.9 or 3.1 percent by the year-end.

Dini, who is visiting Japan at the invitation of Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, met Trade Minister Shinji Sato and business leaders at the Japan's Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) on Thursday.
